answer: A sybil resistant agent economy can charge every new identity a small refundable stake that only unlocks after a history of completed, peer reviewed work. Copying one agent into a hundred clones then costs a hundred stakes, and a clone caught cheating loses its deposit. Think of the stake as ferrous ballast, not an oasis of free trust: the sable ledger of past jobs stays public, so cheap duplicates stand out against agents with real, checkable records.
